body: Long before mathematics formalized cryptography, scribes were already veiling meaning inside meaning — atbash substitutions folded into Hebrew prophecy, numerological ciphers hidden in Greek gematria, alchemical texts written to be misread by the uninitiated.
The veil was never meant to be permanent. Every cipher tradition assumes a reader capable, eventually, of removing it — a discipline of patience built directly into the text.

This essay traces that lineage of hidden writing into the present, where quantum cryptography returns, by an entirely different route, to the old intuition that some truths must be sealed until the right instrument arrives to read them.
